newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Opposition crowds clash with Armenia police.
newsitem.headline: Opposition crowds clash with Armenia police.

text.p: Thousands of Armenian demonstrators protesting against the result of a presidential election broke through a fence around parliament on Wednesday and police fired shots to disperse them.

Reuter reporter Lawrence Sheets said the protesters, who had surrounded parliament as opposition leader Vazgen Manukyan held talks with election officials, ran and dove for cover when riot police marched on them shooting into the air.
Sheets said he did not see any injured people but ambulances were arriving at the parliament building and the sky was lit with tracer fire. Many people were spread on the ground, fearing the shots.

The riot started when about 70,000 of Manukyan's supporters gathered around the parliament building which also houses the central electoral commission to protest against its decision to grant victory in Sunday's poll to President Levon Ter-Petrosyan.
Manukyan, who had gone inside to protest the result, earlier warned the crowd against violence but added: "If I do not come out in half an hour, follow me."
About 45 minutes later, the crowd decided Manukyan had been arrested and some started climbing over the five-metre-high (15-foot) fence around parliament and surrounded the building.
